title: CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
chineseTitle: 第 21 章：调味剂的新风波

paragraphs.en: Anne sighed, placing her slate and books on the kitchen table on June 30th. "There's nothing but goodbyes in this world, as Mrs. Lynde says." She wiped her eyes with a damp handkerchief.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮叹了口气，6月30日这天，她把石板和书放在厨房的桌子上。“这个世界除了告别别无他物，正如雷切尔·林德夫人所说。”她用湿手帕擦了擦眼睛。

paragraphs.en: Marilla replied, "I never thought you were so fond of Mr. Phillips that you needed two handkerchiefs just because he’s leaving."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉回答说：“我从没想过你对菲利普斯先生如此依恋，他走了你就需要两条手帕。”

paragraphs.en: Anne explained, "But I had a presentiment it would be needed today."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮解释说：“但我感到今天需要用到它。”

paragraphs.en: Anne reflected on her tears during Mr. Phillips’s farewell speech. She admitted that she cried not because she was fond of him but because everyone else did. Ruby Gillis started it by bursting into tears, followed by Jane Andrews and others.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在菲利普斯先生告别演讲时的眼泪引起了她的思考。她承认自己并不是因为喜欢他而哭泣，而是因为大家都哭了。鲁比·吉尔思率先落泪，随后简·安德鲁斯等人也跟着哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: Anne tried to hold back, recalling how Mr. Phillips had been sarcastic towards her in class, but eventually gave in. Jane Andrews claimed she wouldn't cry when he left, but ended up borrowing a handkerchief from her brother.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮试图克制自己，想起菲利普斯先生在课堂上对她挖苦讽刺的情景，但最终还是没能忍住。简·安德鲁斯曾声称他走的时候自己不会哭，结果却向哥哥借了一条手帕。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Phillips’s speech was touching, with tears in his eyes. Anne felt remorseful for past misbehaviors and wished she had been more like Minnie Andrews. The girls cried all the way home, with Carrie Sloane repeatedly quoting Mr. Phillips's words to keep them sad.
paragraphs.zh: 菲利普斯先生的讲话感人至深，眼中含着泪光。安妮为自己过去的不当行为感到后悔，她希望自己能像米妮·安德鲁斯那样乖巧些。女孩子们一路哭回家，卡莉·斯洛恩不断引用菲利普斯先生的话来保持她们的情绪低落。

paragraphs.en: Despite feeling sad, Anne found some comfort in the upcoming two-month vacation.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管心中有些伤感，安妮还是在即将来临的两个月假期中找到了一丝慰藉。

paragraphs.en: They met a new minister and his wife coming from the station. Anne couldn’t help but take an interest, despite her sadness over Mr. Phillips leaving. The minister’s wife was pretty, though not regally lovely, as Mrs. Lynde had said about another minister's wife who dressed fashionably.
paragraphs.zh: 她们遇到了新来的牧师和他的妻子，正从车站走来。尽管对菲利普斯先生离开感到难过，安妮还是忍不住产生了兴趣。这位牧师的妻子虽然谈不上倾国倾城，但确实如林德太太所说，长得颇为标致。

paragraphs.en: Their new minister’s wife wore blue muslin with puffed sleeves and a hat trimmed with roses. Anne appreciated the puffed sleeves herself, understanding that the minister’s wife had only recently taken up her role.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的新牧师夫人穿着蓝色的薄纱裙，袖子蓬松，头上戴着玫瑰花装饰的帽子。安妮自己也很欣赏这种蓬松的袖子，理解这位牧师夫人刚刚接手这个职务不久。

paragraphs.en: Marilla went to Mrs. Lynde's that evening to return quilting frames borrowed the previous winter. Many items lent by Mrs. Lynde returned home that night. The arrival of a new minister and his wife sparked curiosity among Avonlea residents, who rarely experienced excitement.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，玛丽拉去雷切尔·林德家归还去年冬天借来的缝纫架。许多由雷切尔·林德借出的物品当晚回到了绿山墙农庄。新牧师及其夫人的到来在埃文利镇居民中引起了好奇，他们很少能体验到这种兴奋感。

paragraphs.en: Old Mr. Bentley, Anne’s former pastor, had been in Avonlea for eighteen years as a widower. Despite gossip linking him to various women each year, he remained unmarried. He resigned in February and left with the community's regrets, though they admired his long service despite his poor preaching skills.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮从前的牧师老本特利先生在埃文利独自生活了十八年。尽管每年都有流言蜚语将他与不同的女性联系在一起，但他始终未娶。二月，他在辞职时带着社区的惋惜之情离开了，虽然大家对他长期的服务表示敬佩，却也承认他的布道技巧并不高明。

paragraphs.en: Since then, Avonlea church hosted numerous trial preachers. These ministers were judged by the congregation, but a small, red-haired girl named Anne shared her opinions with Matthew, while Marilla avoided criticizing them out of principle.
paragraphs.zh: 自那以后，埃文利教堂经常迎来试讲的牧师。这些牧师由会众评判，但一位名叫安妮的小个子红发女孩却向马修倾诉了她的看法，而玛丽拉出于原则上的考虑，没有对他们的表现提出批评。

paragraphs.en: Anne concluded that Mr. Smith wouldn't have been suitable for the position. Mrs. Lynde criticized his poor delivery and lack of imagination, similar to Mr. Bentley’s. Mr. Terry, on the other hand, had too much imagination, which led him astray like Anne in her Haunted Wood incident. Additionally, Mrs. Lynde found his theology unsound.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮得出结论，史密斯先生并不适合这个职位。林德太太批评他糟糕的表达能力和缺乏想象力，这与本特利先生的情况如出一辙。而泰瑞先生则想象力过多，就像安妮在幽灵森林事件中迷失方向一样，最终走上了歧途。此外，林德太太还觉得他的神学观点站不住脚。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Gresham was a good man but lacked dignity due to his humorous stories during sermons. Mr. Marshall seemed attractive, yet Mrs. Lynde deemed him unmarried and unengaged, advising against having an unmarried minister in Avonlea for potential congregation marriage complications. Mrs. Lynde praised Mr. Allan’s interesting sermon and sincere prayers.
paragraphs.zh: 格雷舍姆先生是个好人，但由于他在布道时讲的幽默故事，缺乏庄重感。马歇尔先生看起来很有吸引力，然而林德太太认为他尚未结婚且未订婚，并建议不要在埃文利镇聘任未婚牧师，以防将来会带来一些婚姻上的麻烦。林德太太称赞阿兰先生的精彩布道和真诚祷告。

paragraphs.en: The new minister and his wife were a young, enthusiastic couple still on their honeymoon. They quickly won the hearts of Avonlea residents with their high ideals and cheerful demeanor. Anne fell deeply in love with Mrs. Allan, who was an excellent teacher and allowed students to ask questions freely.
paragraphs.zh: 新来的牧师和他的妻子是一对年轻而充满热情的夫妇，他们正处于蜜月之中。很快，这对夫妇以崇高的理想和乐观的态度赢得了埃文利居民的心。安妮深深地爱上了艾伦太太，她不仅是一位优秀的教师，还允许学生们自由提问。

paragraphs.en: One Sunday afternoon, Anne declared, "Mrs. Allan is perfectly lovely." She admired her for taking over their class and encouraging student participation. Marilla agreed, noting Anne’s knack for asking questions.
paragraphs.zh: 一个周日下午，安妮宣称：“艾伦太太真是个令人赏心悦目的人。”她赞赏艾伦太太接手他们的班级并鼓励学生积极参与。玛丽拉表示赞同，并提到安妮善于提出问题的本领。

paragraphs.en: Anne asked about the Sunday-school picnic, but Marilla thought it inappropriate since the lesson was about Daniel in the lions' den. Despite her skinny frame, Anne wished she had dimples like Mrs. Allan's, who always smiled beautifully. Marilla noted that Anne wasn't as thin now and hoped she would develop some.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮问起了星期天学校野餐的事，但玛丽拉觉得这不太合适，因为那天的课程讲的是但以理在狮穴中的故事。尽管安妮的身材依旧纤瘦，她还是希望自己能像艾伦太太那样拥有可爱的酒窝，因为她总是笑得那么美丽。玛丽拉注意到安妮现在没以前那么瘦了，并希望她能有所变化。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan emphasized the importance of influencing others for good, which made Anne realize religion could be cheerful. She admired Mrs. Allan’s faith but preferred a more joyful approach to being Christian. Marilla then suggested inviting Mr. and Mrs. Allan for tea soon, noting they hadn't visited their house yet.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太强调了影响他人向善的重要性，这让安妮意识到宗教也可以充满欢乐。她钦佩艾伦太太的信仰，但更倾向于一种更加愉悦的基督教生活方式。玛丽拉随后建议她们不久后邀请艾伦夫妇来喝杯茶，指出他们还没有访问过她们家呢。

paragraphs.en: They decided on Wednesday as a suitable day, with Marilla warning Anne not to tell Matthew.
paragraphs.zh: 他们决定将星期三定为合适的日子，玛丽拉警告安妮不要告诉马修。

paragraphs.en: Anne promised secrecy and asked if she could make a cake for the occasion, eager to do something nice for Mrs. Allan. Marilla agreed that Anne could bake a layer cake.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮承诺保密，并询问是否可以为这次聚会做蛋糕，她巴不得能为艾伦太太做点好事。玛丽拉同意让安妮烤一个分层蛋糕。

paragraphs.en: Anne was thrilled about hosting the minister and his wife for tea at Green Gables. She and Diana discussed their plans Tuesday evening by the Dryad's Bubble, creating rainbows with twigs dipped in fir balsam.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮对在绿山墙接待牧师及其夫人喝下午茶感到非常兴奋。周二傍晚，她和戴安娜在干林精的泡泡旁讨论计划，用浸过松脂香油的树枝制造出五彩斑斓的彩虹。

paragraphs.en: Everything was prepared except Anne’s cake and Marilla’s baking-powder biscuits. Anne felt a great sense of responsibility hosting such an important family. They planned to serve jellied chicken, cold tongue, two kinds of jelly, whipped cream, lemon pie, cherry pie, three types of cookies, fruit cake, yellow plum preserves, pound cake, layer cake, and various breads.
paragraphs.zh: 除了安妮的蛋糕和玛丽拉的泡打饼干外，一切准备工作都已经就绪。安妮觉得自己肩负着举办这样一场重要家庭聚会的巨大责任。他们计划供应凉鸡、冷火腿、两种果冻、奶油鲜奶油、柠檬派、樱桃派、三种类型的饼干、水果蛋糕、黄李子果酱、磅蛋糕、分层蛋糕以及各种面包。

paragraphs.en: Anne worried about her layer cake turning out poorly. She dreamed of being chased by a goblin with a layer cake for a head. Diana reassured her that the previous one was excellent.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮担心她的分层蛋糕做不好。她梦见自己被一个头上长着分层蛋糕的小妖精追赶。戴安娜安慰她说，上次做的那个非常好。

paragraphs.en: Despite her fears, Anne trusted in Providence and focused on baking carefully. As they watched rainbows form, she wondered if the dryad would take one as a scarf after they left.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管心中仍有担忧，安妮还是信赖着上帝的安排，并仔细地专心于烘焙。当他们目睹彩虹渐渐形成时，她不禁想象，等她们离开后，林德女巫会不会把彩虹当作围巾带走呢？

paragraphs.en: Anne was excited on Wednesday morning, having caught a cold from dabbling in the spring the night before. Despite this, she focused on baking a cake. She checked if she had forgotten anything and worried about the baking powder's quality.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮星期三一早兴奋不已，前一天晚上她伸手触碰了春水，不小心染上了感冒。尽管如此，她还是全身心地投入到蛋糕烘焙中。她仔细检查是否遗漏了什么步骤，并担心发酵粉的质量。

paragraphs.en: The cake rose beautifully and came out light and feathery. Anne was delighted, imagining Mrs. Allan enjoying it with another piece.
paragraphs.zh: 蛋糕烤得完美无瑕，松软如羽毛。安妮欣喜不已，想象阿兰太太品尝第二片时也会同样享受。

paragraphs.en: "Of course you'll use the best tea set," Anne said to Marilla. "Can I decorate the table with ferns and wild roses?"
paragraphs.zh: “当然你会用最好的茶具，”安妮对玛丽拉说，“我可以把桌上摆上蕨类和野玫瑰吗？”

paragraphs.en: Marilla dismissed her idea as nonsense, insisting that only the food mattered. However, Anne recalled how Mrs. Barry's decorated table impressed the minister, who praised it for both sight and taste.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉一口否定了她的想法，坚持认为只有食物本身才重要。然而，安妮想起巴里太太装饰一新的餐桌曾给牧师留下了深刻印象，他称赞那张桌子既美观又美味。

paragraphs.en: Marilla was determined not to be outdone by Mrs. Barry. She instructed Anne to ensure enough space for dishes and food. Anne used her artistic skills to decorate the tea table with roses and ferns, impressing the minister and his wife.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉决心不让巴里太太占上风。她吩咐安妮要确保有足够的空间摆放餐具和食物。安妮充分发挥她的艺术才能，用玫瑰和蕨类植物装饰了茶桌，给牧师和他的妻子留下了深刻的印象。

paragraphs.en: "Anne's work," Marilla grumbled, but Anne felt elated when Mrs. Allan smiled approvingly.
paragraphs.zh: “安妮的工作，”玛丽拉抱怨道，但当阿兰太太微笑着表示赞同时，安妮感到十分高兴。

paragraphs.en: Matthew attended the gathering reluctantly, dressed in his best clothes under Anne’s encouragement. He talked interestingly to the minister but avoided Mrs. Allan.
paragraphs.zh: 马修在安妮的鼓励下勉强出席了聚会，穿着最好的衣服。他与牧师交谈甚欢，但避开了艾伦太太。

paragraphs.en: The party went smoothly until Anne’s layer cake was served. Mrs. Allan politely declined it, but Marilla, seeing Anne's disappointment, suggested she try a piece.
paragraphs.zh: 聚会进行得很顺利，直到安妮的分层蛋糕端上桌。艾伦太太礼貌地谢绝了，但玛丽拉看到安妮失望的表情，建议她尝一小块。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan and the others sampled the cake. A peculiar expression crossed her face as she ate silently. Marilla tasted the cake and exclaimed at its flavor.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太和其他人品尝了蛋糕。她在默默吃的时候脸上掠过一种奇怪的表情。玛丽拉尝了尝蛋糕，不禁赞叹起它的味道来。

paragraphs.en: "Anne Shirley," Marilla said, "what did you put in this cake?"
paragraphs.zh: “安妮，”玛丽拉问道，“你在这蛋糕里加了些什么？”

paragraphs.en: Anne, mortified after tasting it herself, replied, "Only vanilla, Marilla. It must have been the baking powder."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮在尝过后感到十分尴尬，回答说：“只有香草味，玛丽拉。一定是发酵粉的问题。”

paragraphs.en: Marilla took the bottle of vanilla Anne had used, smelled it, and declared, "Baking powder nonsense! Bring me that bottle."
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉拿起安妮用过的香草瓶，闻了闻，断言道：“胡说八道，是发酵粉！给我把瓶子拿来。”

paragraphs.en: Anne was devastated when Marilla discovered she had flavored the cake with anodyne liniment. "I couldn't smell it—I had such a cold!" she sobbed, fleeing to her room and weeping uncontrollably.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮得知玛丽拉发现她用止痛药膏给蛋糕调味时，心情糟透了。“我根本闻不出来——我感冒得太厉害了！”她抽泣着跑回自己的房间，哭得无法自已。

paragraphs.en: Marilla entered shortly after, finding Anne on her bed. "Oh, Marilla," Anne cried, "I'm disgraced forever. Diana will ask about the cake, and I must tell the truth.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉随后进来，发现安妮躺在床上。“哦，玛丽拉，”安妮喊道，“我永远丢脸了。戴安娜肯定会问起蛋糕的事，我必须说实话。

paragraphs.en: Everyone in Avonlea gossips—schoolboys will laugh at me."
paragraphs.zh: 埃文利镇上的闲言碎语她可承受不起——学校里的男生肯定会取笑我。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan appeared, standing by the bed with a smile. "Suppose you jump up and tell her yourself," she said cheerfully.
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太面带微笑地站在床边说：“要不你干脆起床自己告诉她吧。”她说得轻松愉快。

paragraphs.en: Anne looked up to see Mrs. Allan's amused eyes. "My dear little girl, don't cry like this," she said sincerely, concerned about Anne’s distress. "It's just a funny mistake anyone could make."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮抬头看见阿兰太太带着笑意的眼睛。“我亲爱的小姑娘，别这样哭,”她真诚地说，关切地望着安妮，“这只是任何人都可能犯的一个滑稽的错误。”

paragraphs.en: Anne felt ashamed but admitted, "Yes, I wanted the cake to be perfect for you, Mrs. Allan."
paragraphs.zh: 安妮感到有些羞愧，但还是承认道：“是的，我想让蛋糕完美无缺，太太。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Allan reassured her, "I appreciate your kindness and thoughtfulness. Now, come down with me and show me your flower garden. Miss Cuthbert told me about it—she's very interested in flowers."
paragraphs.zh: 艾伦太太宽慰她说：“我非常感激你的善意和周到。现在，跟我下来，带我去看看你的花圃吧。库伯特小姐跟我说起过这里——她对花草很感兴趣。”

paragraphs.en: Anne felt comforted by Mrs. Allan’s kindness, and they didn’t discuss the liniment cake incident further. Anne realized she had enjoyed the evening more than expected despite the earlier trouble. She sighed deeply.
paragraphs.zh: 安妮感到欣慰的是艾伦太太的善意，两人并未再提及那块润肤饼的事情。尽管之前有些波折，但安妮发现自己实际上比预期中更享受这个晚上。她深深地叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: "Marilla, isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes?"
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，不是觉得明天是个全新的开始，没有任何遗憾吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I'll warrant you'll make plenty," Marilla replied. "You're always making mistakes, Anne."
paragraphs.zh: “你肯定会出不少差错，”玛丽拉回答，“你总是搞错了。”

paragraphs.en: "Yes, and I know it," Anne admitted mournfully. "But have you noticed one encouraging thing about me? I never repeat the same mistake twice."
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我知道这一点，”安妮悲伤地承认道，“但是你有没有注意到我身上有一点让人欣慰的地方？那就是我从不重蹈覆辙。”

paragraphs.en: "Maybe not, but that doesn't help much when you keep making new ones."
paragraphs.zh: “也许不行，但你不停地试新口味也帮不上什么忙。”

paragraphs.en: "Oh, Marilla, there must be a limit to my mistakes. When I reach the end of them, I'll be through with them," Anne said optimistically.
paragraphs.zh: “玛丽拉，我的错误总该有个限度吧。等我走到尽头，也就和它们划清界限了。”安妮充满希望地说。

paragraphs.en: Marilla dismissed her thoughts and told her to give the cake to the pigs; it wasn’t fit for human consumption, even Jerry Boute’s.
paragraphs.zh: 玛丽拉把这些想法抛在脑后，吩咐安妮把蛋糕给猪吃；就连伯特家的猪也不配吃这么好的东西。
